newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to cut state budget by 50 bln baht a year.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to cut state budget by 50 bln baht a year.

text.p: Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan told the Thai cabinet on Tuesday that he would cut the annual government budget by at least 50 billion baht ($2.0 billion) a year in 1997 and 1998 in a move to improve the economy.

Amnuay told cabinet ministers that the government would delay low priority public projects especially those which require heavy foreign exchange spending and it also planned to trim military expenditure.

The spokesman said Amnuay proposed to the cabinet that the government would encourage its people to tap only essential long-term foreign loans while measures would be implemented to trim wasteful consumer spending.

Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Monday he would ask Thai Airways International Plc to consider leasing aircraft to meet its expansion requirement instead of going ahead with a plan to place orders for 21 new aircraft during 1996-2000.
The spokesman said Amnuay sought to mobilise more domestic public savings and give a greater role to private investors in major infrastructure projects.
